test_cases.task: Track the personal Flow config in the source repository

input.description: Track the personal alias configuration in the Flow source repository and provide an integrated export/import workflow.
input.context: The active config is a single JSON file with no current secrets; runtime scheduler state must remain local.

criteria: Flow exposes config export and import commands
The repository tracks the current personal config as flow.config.json
Export validates and atomically updates the snapshot
Import validates and migrates before atomically replacing the active config
Runtime history, locks, temporary files, and scheduler logs are excluded
All Go tests, race checks for config, and go vet pass
key_behaviors: Running flow config export from the source root updates flow.config.json
Invalid snapshots never overwrite the active config
Git commit and push remain part of the normal source repository workflow

test_cases.task: Optimize the Flow web UI and concurrent run output

input.description: Optimize the current Flow UI implementation without breaking CRUD, scheduling, or streamed run output.
input.context: The existing page is a dependency-free embedded HTML/CSS/JavaScript application with a new multi-tab output panel.

criteria: Only the selected resource section is visible
Concurrent runs retain independent Stop button and output-tab state
Unexpected stream closure cannot leave a run permanently marked running
Dynamic aliases are safely passed through data attributes instead of inline JavaScript
The layout is responsive and keyboard focus is visible
Modal and output tabs expose appropriate accessibility semantics
Go tests, UI race tests, JavaScript syntax validation, and local UI/API smoke tests pass
key_behaviors: Escape closes an open modal before stopping the active run
Arrow keys switch between output tabs
Finished output tabs can be cleared without interrupting running tabs
Reload, save, delete, and API failures use non-blocking status feedback

test_cases.task: Remove unused tmux functionality from Flow

input.description: Remove Flow's tmux and layout functionality because the remote shell already provides splitting and there is no current use case.
input.context: The removal must cover the CLI, configuration schema, lazy dispatch, picker and chain workflows, Web UI/API, tests, and documentation while preserving all non-layout personal configuration.

criteria: The layout and up commands are no longer registered
Script execution no longer exposes in-tmux or session flags
The layout schema, tmux driver, UI tab, and layouts API are removed
Schema v1 migrates to v2 by dropping legacy layouts while preserving supported resources
The active config and tracked snapshot validate at schema v2 without a layouts field
All Go tests, focused race checks, go vet, build, and JavaScript syntax validation pass
key_behaviors: flow layout and flow up return unknown-command errors
Lazy dispatch and interactive workflows cover scripts, cmds, greps, finds, and jumps only
Projects, scripts, cmds, greps, finds, and schedules survive migration unchanged
